concepts.name: 한 모노그램
concepts.prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create ONE polished design-review board for 한녕 (Hannyeong), a macOS Korean-English automatic input method. Mature, precise, understated software identity, absolutely not cute. Wide 3:2 white/light-neutral canvas. On the left, a large final app-icon concept (rounded-square tile, clean margins). On the right, show the EXACT SAME mark isolated in solid BLACK, without any tile/background, as the matching menu-bar icon concept; keep its geometry simple enough for 16px. Neat generous spacing, straight-on orthographic presentation, crisp flat vector-like graphics. No 3D bevel, keycap gloss, texture, mascot, eyes, smile, whimsical forms, gradients, decorative background, watermarks or extraneous labels. Only render text when the individual concept explicitly needs it. The two views must be the SAME identity, not two different marks. Concept 1: Korean-led typographic identity. A warm ivory app tile bearing one BLACK, strongly constructed Korean syllable "한", exactly correct Hangul spelling. Design the glyph as a compact architectural stencil: squared terminals, equal thick strokes, clear rectangular ㄴ at the bottom, carefully spaced ㅎ and ㅏ, generous circular counter only where the Korean glyph requires it. No curves underneath or friendly flourishes. One small sharply cut interruption in the horizontal stroke makes it distinctive as a custom mark rather than an ordinary system font. The right-hand menu version is the same compact black 한 stencil. Only text is the glyph 한. Very restrained typographic Swiss/Korean editorial feel.

Concept 5: Literal bilingual identity using the exact Korean consonant "ㅎ" and a Latin uppercase "A". Slate-charcoal app tile, pale ivory mark.
